transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-19
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Jordan Park (Redwood Solutions Eng - joined later), Lina Morales (Head of ML - Northbridge), Samir Patel (Platform Eng - Northbridge), Dana Lee (PM - Northbridge)

Auto-generated summary: short demo and Q&A. Some transcription errors present.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Hi Lina, Samir, Dana, good to see you. We're gonna walk through JSON-mode structured output, guardrails for tool calling, and show the Console flow + Optimize suggestions. Ethan will lead the deep-dive.
[00:18] Lina: Thanks Maya. We're mostly interested how we can guarantee the output shape for downstream services and avoid hallucinated tool calls. We're migrating parts of our assist pipeline and need strict contracts.
[00:30] Ethan: Totally. We'll show an API-first demo and then flip to the Console to show per-route schema enforcement and built-in validation errors. Quick note: some of my slides say "Redwood Opti-mize" because of a font render, sorry about that.
[00:45] Samir: Two quick constraints from infra side: 1) we need VPC peering and allowlist, 2) we might want a dedicated pool if latency needs are <40ms P50.
[00:58] Maya: Good, we'll call those out as we go.

--- Demo: API + JSON mode walk-through ---
[01:12] Ethan: Opening the API playground. First example: a simple tool-calling schema - you see the JSON schema on the right. We set "required" fields name, timestamp and payload.items[]. The runtime will reject responses that don't match, returning a structured validation error with a code and a suggestion.
[01:40] Dana: So the model itself can't return malformed JSON? What happens if it returns free text?
[01:48] Ethan: Two layers: 1) the model is prompted to emit JSON only (we use a strict system prompt and examples), 2) Redwood's schema enforcer validates the output post-generation. If it doesn't match, we have configurable policies: fail-fast (return error), attempt repair (re-run a constrained completion), or emit best-effort plus diagnostics. You can configure per-route.
[02:10] Lina: Repair attempts — is that deterministic? We worry about flapping outputs during low confidence.
[02:18] Ethan: Repair is deterministic in the sense the same policy will re-run with a tighter temperature and structural enforcement tokens; but it's not a cryptographic guarantee. For strictness, you pin route policy to "reject" and route to a fallback processor.
[02:35] Samir: Can you show how this looks over the network? We want to validate on our side too.
[02:40] Ethan: Sure. cURL example: POST /v1/generate with schema field and x-redwood-route header. Response will include a "schema_validation" block with status: "ok" or "invalid" and a small error array. I'll paste the snippet after.
[02:58] Maya: We'll put the example snippet in the chat.

[03:10] Ethan: Switching to a complex example: multi-tool workflow. The model can return a tool_call object with tool_name, args structured per schema. Console shows a live trace: model output, tool invocation, tool response, final decision.
[03:30] Jordan (joined): sorry folks, had to jump in—seen a few of these. Important: our SDKs include strongly-typed bindings so your infra can deserialize tool args safely.
[03:45] Dana: Are the tool calls synchronous or push-based? We need async for long-running ops.
[03:52] Ethan: Both. You can mark tools as sync or async in the catalog. For async, Redwood returns a task_id and you can poll or subscribe to webhook events. The Console shows a redaction workflow for sensitive tool args.

--- Console walk-through ---
[04:20] Ethan: Console -> Routes. Here we show a route for "order-enrichment" pinned to model v1.2-quant. Look at the per-route schema toggle. You can set failure policy, max retries, and cost cap.
[04:40] Samir: Cost cap — how granular is that? We need per-customer cost tracking and token-level attribution.
[04:47] Maya: Console exposes token-level cost breakdown and you can attach a quota to an API key. Also recommends batching settings from Optimize based on your seq distribution.
[04:58] Lina: Speaking of Optimize, how does it recommend quantization? We run a sensitivity test on our prompts.
[05:06] Ethan: Optimize analyzes latency/quality/price from historical traces and suggests quantization profiles and batch sizes. It also simulates cost per 1M tokens at different settings. For your workload we expect 20-30% cost reduction with int8 quant on our serving runtime, but we recommend running the suggested small benchmark first.
[05:28] Dana: Benchmark steps - does Redwood provide the harness?
[05:33] Maya: Yes, a benchmark spreadsheet + a turnkey runner we can grant access to. We'll include a pre-filled config for your sample prompts.

--- Security & compliance Qs ---
[05:50] Samir: A few enterprise controls: SSO/SAML, RBAC with org-scoped roles, KMS integration for model keys, and audit logs.
[05:58] Ethan: All supported. Private deployments support customer-managed KMS and HSM options. Audit logs are exportable to your SIEM. We have a SOC 2 report you can request; I think Jordan has the link.
[06:10] Jordan: I'll paste the SOC2 + ISO docs. Note: Private control plane in VPC gives you more egress controls.
[06:20] Lina: For data residency, we may need EU-only hosting. Is that possible?
[06:25] Maya: Yes — regional routing can pin requests to EU regions and you can choose Private deployments in a region.

--- Live tool-calling example ---
[06:40] Ethan: I'm going to run a live demo. Prompt: "Create a shipping label and call the shipping_tool with args schema." Sending request...
[06:55] Ethan: Response shows tool_call: {tool_name: "shipping_tool", args: {order_id: "NB-3321", address: {line1: ...}}} — note: we enforce address schema shape and postcode pattern. Console shows validation ok.
[07:12] Samir: Could the model try to call "payment_tool" by mistake? We need a whitelist.
[07:18] Ethan: You can set tool_allowlist per-route; any call to a non-whitelisted tool is either rejected or mapped to a safe no-op.
[07:25] Dana: What about secrets in args — credit card numbers etc.
[07:30] Ethan: Redwood masks PII automatically per schema annotations (format: "credit_card"), and we also redact tokens in the UI. For Private deployments you can toggle encryption-in-transit and at-rest with your KMS.

[07:45] Lina: Can you show a failed schema validation and the repair flow?
[07:50] Ethan: Sure — I'm going to force a malformed address by changing the schema minLength. Send...
[08:05] Ethan: Console shows validation failed, policy = "attempt_repair", the system re-grounded with explicit slot-filling prompts and returned a corrected JSON. You see the trace: original, repair attempt (temp=0.2), final.
[08:20] Lina: The repair attempt added a default postal_code of "00000" — that's risky. Can we avoid defaults?
[08:25] Ethan: Yes, you can set a no-defaults flag in the route. Good catch.

[08:40] Samir: On performance: we'd like to run a 48-hour sustained load sim. What support do you provide?
[08:47] Maya: For Dedicated customers we provide a pilot reserved pool and support to run the soak test. We'll allocate an engineer to help run the harness.
[08:55] Samir: Are there SLAs on tail latency?
[08:58] Ethan: For Dedicated we offer SLA-backed P95 targets per model class. Hosted has best-effort but we provide latency hysteresis and automatic fallback to cheaper variants.

--- Objections and tradeoffs ---
[09:15] Dana: We're concerned about cost if we keep retries on repair turned on — that can double token usage.
[09:22] Ethan: Yep, which is why Optimize gives you predicted additional tokens from repair policies. You can set a hard token budget per-call.
[09:30] Lina: If we choose private deployment, how much work is the on-prem package?
[09:35] Maya: Our private package is a Helm chart + operator. Typical install with infra team takes 2-3 weeks plus network config. Jordan: we usually do a workshop and we offer an install-runbook.
[09:46] Jordan: Also recommend using our Kafka-backed event streaming for async tool hooks to keep latency decoupled.

--- Integration points & developer experience ---
[10:05] Ethan: SDK examples: TypeScript binding shows typed tool args, and Python SDK has a validate_and_call helper. We'll share a repo with examples for your stack.
[10:15] Dana: Will we get an API key per microservice?
[10:18] Maya: You can generate API keys per-service and attach RBAC policies and quotas. Keys can be rotated via Console or API.

--- Pricing & procurement ---
[10:30] Maya: Pricing: hosted per-token plus embedding ops. Dedicated is committed monthly blocks; we can run numbers for your 1M token/mo estimate. I'll send a dedicated vs hosted cost comparison.
[10:40] Samir: Is there a minimum committed spend for Dedicated?
[10:43] Maya: Yes, usually a 3-month minimum for pilot reserved pools. We'll include exact tiers.

--- Open technical questions ---
[10:55] Lina: How deterministic is schema validation across model versions? If we move models, will strictness change?
[11:00] Ethan: Validation is separate from the model and deterministic. But model behavior around ambiguity can still vary; we recommend tying a route to a model version and rolling when you validate on your eval set.
[11:12] Dana: Any gotchas with streaming and JSON mode?
[11:16] Ethan: Streaming will chunk tokens; we buffer until valid JSON parse. If streaming fails parse mid-way, Console shows partial tokens and you can opt to do final-parse validation.

--- Closing and recap ---
[11:30] Maya: Quick recap: 1) we'll send schema examples + repair policy docs; 2) Ethan will share SDK snippets and sample repo; 3) we'll propose a Dedicated pilot for your latency test; 4) Jordan will share compliance docs. Any final questions?
[11:50] Samir: Please include the IP ranges we'll need to whitelist.
[11:54] Maya: Added to action items.
[12:00] Lina: Good session. When can we do the POC kickoff?
[12:05] Maya: Propose Wed 2025-02-26, 10am PT. We'll aim for infra + ML engs.
[12:12] Dana: Works for us.
[12:18] Jordan: I'll drop links in the follow-up: SOC2, SDK repo, bench harness, and the Console route JSON example.

[12:30] End meeting.
